revenue_segments.name: Entertainment
revenue_segments.commentary: Segment operating income rose 64% in the quarter to $1,680M from $1,022M, driven by subscription and affiliate fees ($7,545M vs $6,765M, up 12%). That growth included 4 points from the Fubo Transaction, 3 points from higher effective rates, 3 points from more subscribers and 1 point from FX. Advertising revenue fell (4% lower rates, partly offset by impressions and Fubo). Nine-month operating income rose only 3% to $4,116M from $3,983M as operating expenses rose 9%. A+E impairment charges of $812M and severance of $60M in the quarter sit outside segment operating income.

revenue_segments.name: Sports
revenue_segments.commentary: Segment operating income fell 17% to $858M from $1,037M as higher programming and production costs outweighed higher subscription and affiliate fees. The NBA contract renewal shifted costs from the first half into Q3. Nine-month operating income fell 14% to $1,701M from $1,971M. Prior-year UFC pay-per-view revenue did not repeat because the UFC rights expired in December 2025.

revenue_segments.name: Experiences
revenue_segments.commentary: Operating income rose 20% to $3,017M from $2,516M, which implies about a 57% incremental margin in the quarter. Operating expenses rose 5% and depreciation and amortization rose 15% to $821M, partly on Disney Cruise Line additions. Domestic Parks & Experiences operating income was $2,088M vs $1,650M (+27%). Nine-month revenue was $29,461M (+8%) and operating income $8,941M vs $8,117M (+10%).

key_risks.description: Sports segment profitability is eroding. Operating income fell 17% in the quarter and 14% over nine months as programming and production costs outran revenue growth of 4% and 2%. The NBA renewal shifted costs into Q3 from the first half, so the nine-month decline is the cleaner run-rate. UFC pay-per-view revenue also rolled off after the rights expired in December 2025.

Carriage dispute exposure: in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, NFL Network and NFL RedZone were removed from Comcast Xfinity and service has not been reinstated. This threatens distribution and subscription and affiliate fee revenue tied to the NFL arrangements.

Shareholder returns are running ahead of cash generation. Nine-month repurchases of $7,245M plus dividends of $1,337M (about $8.6B) exceed free cash flow of roughly $5.7B (cash provided by operations of $12,515M less $6,780M of investments in parks, resorts and other property). Borrowings rose $3,689M, and commercial paper with original maturities greater than three months rose to $3,712M from $99M. This leaves the balance sheet to absorb the gap against a target of at least $9B of fiscal 2026 buybacks.

Operating cash flow declined from $13,627M to $12,515M over nine months, with income tax payments a major drag (income taxes change in operating assets and liabilities of $(1,611)M vs $(136)M). Cash taxes and higher capex of about $9B in fiscal 2026 compress free cash flow.

Large impairment and restructuring charges sit outside segment operating income: $1,139M for nine months vs $437M, including $812M for the A+E investment impairment and $60M of severance in the quarter. The A+E write-down signals weakness in linear network assets, and recurring charges make segment profit look cleaner than GAAP results.

Experiences growth is leaning on price. Of 9% admissions growth, 5 points came from per-capita ticket revenue and 3 points from attendance. Operating expenses rose 6% over nine months, and depreciation and amortization rose 15% on cruise ship additions. A consumer slowdown or softer international demand would expose the price-led margin gains and the rising capital intensity.

Entertainment advertising and content sales are soft, and the fee growth driving segment profit is flattered by the Fubo Transaction (4 of 12 points). Nine-month Entertainment operating income grew only 3% on 7% revenue growth, so durability of the quarter's +64% operating income jump is unproven.

Debt and capital intensity are rising. The current portion of borrowings is $8,627M, short-term commercial paper issuance is increasing, and fiscal 2026 capex is expected at about $9B against $8B in fiscal 2025.

bull_case: Experiences is compounding: Q3 FY26 operating income rose 20% to $3,017M on 10% revenue growth, with domestic Parks & Experiences operating income up 27% to $2,088M. Quarterly margin expanded about 260bp and the incremental margin was roughly 57%.

Growth in the parks is not purely price. Admissions rose 9% (5 points per-capita ticket revenue, 3 points attendance), resorts and vacations rose 17% on new cruise capacity, and domestic attendance grew 3% even with international headwinds.

Entertainment profit inflected: operating income rose 64% to $1,680M on subscription and affiliate fees up 12% to $7,545M, with 3 points from rate and 3 points from subscribers beyond the Fubo contribution. This points to real pricing and scale effects in streaming.

Management is returning capital aggressively: $7,245M of buybacks and $1,337M of dividends over nine months, a target of at least $9B of fiscal 2026 buybacks, and diluted shares down to 1,743M from 1,805M year over year.

Liquidity is ample, with $12,250M of undrawn committed bank capacity and $5,185M of cash, while capex of about $9B is building cruise, domestic and international capacity that should support volume growth into fiscal 2027.
Fiscal 2026 segment operating income growth is guided to be back-half weighted, which sets up Q4 and fiscal 2027 comparisons as cruise ships (Destiny, Adventure) and the film slate ramp.
bear_case: GAAP earnings quality is weaker than segment results: diluted EPS fell to $1.51 from $2.92 and nine-month net income fell to $7,793M from $11,988M on a prior-year non-cash Hulu tax benefit and $900M of quarterly restructuring and impairment charges (A+E, severance). Nine-month charges were $1,139M vs $437M.

Sports is deteriorating: operating income fell 17% in the quarter and 14% over nine months while revenue grew only 4% and 2%. Rights-cost inflation and the NBA cost shift distort the quarter, and the UFC rights expired in December 2025.

Capital returns exceed free cash flow. Buybacks plus dividends of about $8.6B vs roughly $5.7B of free cash flow was funded in part by a $3,689M rise in borrowings, including a jump in longer-dated commercial paper. Operating cash flow fell 8% on higher cash taxes.

Entertainment's +64% quarter is not confirmed by nine-month operating income growth of only 3%. Fee growth is flattered by 4 points from Fubo, and advertising and content sales are declining, so the first-half base was weak.

Experiences leverage is peaking: the nine-month incremental margin was about 40% vs 57% in Q3, first-half operating income growth was only about 6%, and depreciation and amortization is up 15%. Growth is price-led (5 points price vs 3 points attendance) and exposed to a consumer slowdown.
Carriage risk: NFL Network and NFL RedZone were removed from Comcast Xfinity in Q3 with no reinstatement, a risk to affiliate fee revenue.
Rising capital intensity (capex of about $9B vs $8B) and about $24B of content spend reduce free cash flow flexibility, leaving buybacks reliant on balance sheet capacity.

what_to_watch.text:
**Experiences Momentum and Outlook Revision:** Experiences operating income rose 20% to $3,017M on 10% revenue growth, led by domestic Parks & Experiences (+27% to $2,088M). The quarterly incremental margin was roughly 57%, and admissions grew 9% on both price and volume, which supports the case for an upside revision to the fiscal 2026 outlook. However, nine-month operating income grew only 10% (about 40% incremental margin), implied first-half growth was only about 6%, and depreciation and amortization rose 15% on cruise additions, so Q3 may be the high-water mark rather than a run-rate.

-> Monitor the Q4 Experiences incremental margin, depreciation and amortization growth from the cruise fleet, and whether management raises or merely reaffirms the back-half weighted outlook.

**Parks Pricing vs. Volume and the Capex Ramp:** Of the 9% growth in theme park admissions, 5 points came from per-capita ticket revenue and 3 points from attendance, while nine-month Experiences operating expenses rose 6% (other operating expense up 15%) and parks investments rose to $6,780M from $6,108M. That pattern leaves margins exposed if the consumer softens or pricing elasticity breaks, and the NYT and CNBC both flag mounting macro uncertainty and slower visitor trends. That said, attendance is still growing 3% domestically, cruise capacity is directly feeding resort revenue (+17%), and the capex is building capacity that should support volume growth later.

-> Monitor domestic attendance versus per-capita spending, international attendance trends, and the return profile management ties to fiscal 2026 capex of about $9B.

**Capital Return Funding:** Nine-month buybacks of $7,245M and dividends of $1,337M total about $8.6B, versus roughly $5.7B of free cash flow ($12,515M of operating cash flow less $6,780M of parks investment). Borrowings rose $3,689M, commercial paper over three months rose to $3,712M from $99M, and the company is targeting at least $9B of fiscal 2026 buybacks alongside about $9B of capex and about $24B of content spend. On the other hand, the company holds $5,185M of cash and $12,250M of undrawn bank capacity, so the shortfall is a capital allocation choice rather than a liquidity constraint, and operating cash flow was depressed by higher cash tax payments.

-> Monitor Q4 operating cash flow, the net change in borrowings and commercial paper, and management commentary on how much of the $9B buyback is funded by free cash flow versus balance sheet capacity.

**Sports Segment Profitability:** Sports operating income fell 17% to $858M in the quarter and 14% to $1,701M over nine months, as higher programming and production costs outweighed subscription and affiliate fee growth on revenue up just 4% and 2%. The NBA renewal shifted costs from the first half into Q3, so the quarter overstates the decline, but the nine-month drop is the cleaner signal and is still negative; prior-year UFC pay-per-view revenue has also rolled off. That said, revenue is growing on fees and advertising, ESPN's direct-to-consumer launch is nearly a year old, and NBA and NHL playoff ratings were strong. NFL Network and RedZone also remain off Comcast Xfinity.

-> Monitor Q4 Sports operating income against rights-cost timing, any resolution of the NFL carriage dispute, and commentary on ESPN direct-to-consumer economics.

**Entertainment Profit Durability:** Entertainment operating income jumped 64% to $1,680M, driven by subscription and affiliate fees up 12% to $7,545M (3 points from rate, 3 points from subscribers, 4 points from the Fubo Transaction). However, nine-month operating income grew only 3% to $4,116M on 7% revenue growth with operating expenses up 9%, implying first-half operating income down roughly 18%, while advertising fell on 4% lower rates and content sales declined. Organic fee growth excluding Fubo is closer to 7%, so the quarter may reflect a weak base and timing rather than a durable inflection.

-> Monitor organic subscription and affiliate fee growth after Fubo laps, advertising rate trends, and Q4 Entertainment operating income versus the 64% quarterly jump.

**Impairments, Restructuring and Earnings Quality:** Restructuring and impairment charges rose to $1,139M for nine months from $437M, including $812M for the A+E investment impairment and $60M for severance in the quarter, and these items are excluded from segment operating income. Net income fell to $2,844M from $5,943M in the quarter, partly on the prior-year non-cash Hulu tax benefit, so the GAAP picture is much weaker than segment profit suggests. That said, the A+E charge is non-cash, and the cash cost is limited to severance, so the cash impact is smaller than the headline.

-> Monitor further impairments of linear network investments, the split between cash severance and non-cash write-downs, and the reconciliation from segment operating income to GAAP results.

**Back-Half Weighting and Cost Timing:** Management has framed fiscal 2026 segment operating income growth as primarily back-half weighted, citing timing of cruise expenses, the film slate and marketing, and sports rights payments. The Disney Destiny (November 2025) and Disney Adventure (March 2026) launches add capacity and depreciation, and the film slate includes Toy Story 5. However, theatrical marketing and the Fubo Transaction already lifted selling, general, administrative and other costs, and capex is rising to about $9B, so cost timing could absorb part of the revenue upside.

-> Monitor Q4 and early fiscal 2027 commentary on cruise launch costs, theatrical marketing, sports rights payments, and any change to the back-half weighting language.

**Streaming Franchise and Linear Decline Offset:** CNBC reports Entertainment streaming revenue up 11% to $5.53B, helped by subscribers, price hikes and advertising, and the bundle strategy is intended to offset traditional TV declines. However, Disney has stopped reporting some metrics, such as linear network revenue and operating income breakdowns and subscriber counts, which limits the ability to verify streaming profitability, and the A+E impairment points to linear erosion.

-> Monitor any disclosure of streaming operating income, subscriber or engagement metrics, and the pace of linear network revenue decline on the call.

hypotheses_explored.question: Is the Experiences margin expansion that the Street is cheering actually volume-driven, or is it price-driven and vulnerable to a consumer slowdown that would also expose rising cost and capex burdens?
hypotheses_explored.summary: Q3 FY26 evidence shows Experiences growth leaning on pricing: attendance grew about 3% while per-capita ticket revenue added about 5%, and cruise capacity expansion is carrying resort revenue. Operating expenses grew 6% over nine months with other operating expense up 15%, and parks capex rose to $6.78B from $6.11B. The bull case assumes pricing elasticity holds and capex converts to returns on schedule; this is a hypothesis to test on the call, not a short thesis.
